label: rem:trace-locality-gs-reconciliation
title: Locality after normalisation: digesting global entanglement
html: Two computational operations seemingly contradict: single Hecke crossings obey Markov locality, yet composite braid evaluation via Gröbner–Shirshov reduction is non-local. Markov locality of single Hecke crossings separates them: the GS algorithm digests global entanglement into the coefficients of the normal form, and the trace is evaluated afterwards. Whether that evaluation is local over the normal form, a product of per-letter factors, is not yet proved; the product-factorisation check records what has been verified.
